dish: Tsukemen dipped in a rich pork-and-seafood broth simmered for 13 hours
n: Rokurinsha, Tokyo Ramen Street (六厘舎 東京ラーメンストリート)
address: Tokyo Ramen Street, Tokyo Station First Avenue B1 (Yaesu side), Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
w: The star of Tokyo Station's eight-shop Tokyo Ramen Street and by far its longest queue — thick tsukemen noodles dipped into a dense pork-and-seafood broth simmered for 13 hours.

dish: Old-school Tokyo shōyu ramen with chewy noodles and fried onions, gyoza on the side
n: Chūkamen-ten Kiraku, Dōgenzaka (中華麺店 喜楽)
w: A Dōgenzaka relic serving Tokyo-style noodles since 1952 — shōyu ramen with chewy noodles and crisp fried onions, regulars coming back for decades.

dish: Shrimp tsukemen — shrimp-miso and shrimp-tomato dipping broths made from leftover shrimp shells
n: Tsukemen Gonokami Seisakusho (つけ麺 五ノ神製作所)
address: Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo (by Shinjuku Station south side)
w: Queues form an hour before opening for this shrimp-obsessed tsukemen counter, whose creamy shrimp-miso and shrimp-tomato dips are built from hundreds of kilos of otherwise-wasted shrimp shells.

dish: Hakata tonkotsu ramen — milky pork-bone broth with ultra-thin flat noodles
n: Akanoren, Nishi-Azabu (赤のれん)
w: Founded in 1946 as the first Hakata-style ramen shop in the Kantō region; a late-night Nishi-Azabu institution for milky tonkotsu and ultra-thin flat noodles.

dish: Mabo ramen — noodles under fiery, numbing Sichuan mapo tofu
n: Shibire Noodles Rousokuya, Ginza (SHIBIRE NOODLE 蝋燭屋)
w: A chic Ginza noodle bar run by a former Chinese-restaurant chef, specialising in ma-la heat: mabo ramen crowned with numbing mapo tofu.

dish: Rustic shōyu ramen; shōyu/shio/white-shōyu tsukemen limited to 10 a day
n: Ramenya Shima, Nishi-Shinjuku (らぁ麺や 嶋)
w: Ranked No 1 on Ramen Adventures' best-100 for 2025 and a fixture of Tabelog's Tokyo top three — queues once began at 7am; the rustic shōyu ramen is the bowl to get.

dish: Double-soup (duck + seafood) chūka soba with a punchy shōyu tare
n: Chūka Soba Shibata, Komae (中華そば しば田)
w: A celebrated chūka-soba champion that relocated to Komae; its duck-and-seafood double soup and punchy soy tare put it at No 4 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 Tokyo best-100.

dish: Shōyu or shio chūka soba on kombu, dried-fish, duck and Shamo-chicken stock
n: Chūka Soba Kamofuku, Hachiōji (中華そば 鴨福)
address: Hachiōji, Tokyo (15 min walk from Hachiōji Station)
w: Western Tokyo's most raved-about ramen of 2024 per Time Out and No 5 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 best-100 — worth the trek from Hachiōji Station for its duck-and-Shamo chūka soba.

dish: Kirby-shaped burgers and pizza; each dish comes with a gift (plate, figurine, coaster or mug)
n: Kirby Café Tokyo, Tokyo Solamachi (カービィカフェ)
address: Tokyo Solamachi 4F, Tokyo Skytree Town, Oshiage, Sumida-ku, Tokyo
w: Nintendo's pink hero gets his own café on Solamachi's fourth floor under Skytree — Kirby-shaped burgers and pizza, most dishes and drinks served with a collectible, plus an exclusive-goods shop.
anime: Kirby (Nintendo / HAL Laboratory) — the official character café

dish: Tasting counters from ham and sausages to Japanese oden; Café Prunier Paris caviar and champagne
n: Isetan Shinjuku Depachika (伊勢丹新宿店 食品フロア)
address: Isetan Shinjuku main store B1, 3-14-1 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
w: The flagship Isetan's basement food hall — one of Tokyo's poshest depachika, renovated in 2023, with a fresh market of tasting counters (ham, sausage, oden) and Café Prunier Paris for caviar and champagne.

dish: Ready-made deli, wagashi and Western sweets on B2; one of Tokyo's best cheese counters and flawless Japanese fruit on B3
n: Ginza Mitsukoshi Depachika (銀座三越 食品フロア)
address: Ginza Mitsukoshi B2–B3, Ginza 4-chōme, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
w: Two basement floors under Ginza's landmark department store: B2 for prepared food, Japanese and Western sweets and bakeries; B3 a gourmet supermarket with an outstanding cheese counter and perfect Japanese fruit.

dish: Oden simmered in a light dashi, served since 1915
n: Asakusa Oden Otafuku (浅草おでん 大多福)
w: Founded in 1915 and one of Tokyo's oldest oden houses — paper lanterns, a kept garden and pots of oden simmering in light dashi; a former Michelin Bib Gourmand.

dish: Grilled-then-steamed unagi with a sauce unchanged for some 220 years
n: Unagi Komagata Maekawa (駒形 前川)
address: Komagata, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (on the Sumida River near Asakusa Station)
w: An Edo-period eel wholesaler turned restaurant on the Sumida riverbank: unagi grilled and steamed until fluffy, lacquered with a tare the house says has not changed in 220 years.

dish: Tendon (tempura over rice) and tempura sets
n: Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa (大黒家天麩羅)
address: Near Sensō-ji (Denbōin-dōri side), Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
w: A stone's throw from Sensō-ji, the best known of Asakusa's old tempura houses (alongside San Sada and Owariya), with queues for its tempura and tendon.

dish: Customisable Hakata tonkotsu ramen eaten in solo booths
n: Ichiran Shibuya (一蘭 渋谷店)
w: The Fukuoka tonkotsu chain famous for customising noodle firmness, richness, garlic and spring onion on a paper form and slurping alone in a partitioned booth — a rite of passage for first-time visitors.

dish: Single-origin pour-over and espresso at Blue Bottle's first store outside the US
n: Blue Bottle Coffee Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Flagship
w: Blue Bottle's first café outside the US (2015), set in a converted warehouse — its arrival made Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Tokyo's specialty-coffee neighbourhood.

dish: Agemanjū (deep-fried bean-paste buns) and seasonal wagashi, in a 1930 shop
n: Takemura, Kanda-Sudachō (竹むら)
w: A 1930 sweets parlour that escaped wartime damage and still trades from its original wooden building, a designated historic structure — famous for agemanjū and old-school wagashi.

dish: Hand-kneaded, rolled and cut soba; yuba (tofu-skin) soba and mitsuba soba
n: Dashin Soan, Shimokitazawa (打心蕎庵)
address: Residential street ~10 min walk from Shimokitazawa Station, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
w: A traditional house with a small garden on a quiet Shimokitazawa backstreet, drawing soba connoisseurs from across the city for hand-cut noodles — try the yuba soba or mitsuba soba.

dish: Vienna coffee (espresso topped with whipped cream)
n: Ladrio (ラドリオ)
w: Jimbōchō kissaten opened in 1949 in a narrow alley of the book town, a long-standing literary hangout; credited with introducing Vienna coffee to Japan.

dish: Morning set: coffee with butter toast
n: Sabouru (さぼうる)
w: Iconic Jimbōchō kissaten in business since 1955, known for its cottage-style front and tiki-like interior crammed with trinkets gifted by regulars.

dish: Egg sandwich (tamago-sando) with coffee
n: Kayaba Coffee (カヤバ珈琲)
w: Kissaten in a 1916 Yanaka building, run as a coffee shop from 1938 to 2006 and reopened in 2009 with the original exterior and signage; known for its egg sandwich.

dish: Hand-poured single-origin coffee (around ten bean varieties)
n: Arise Coffee Roasters (アライズコーヒーロースターズ)
w: Small single-origin roaster in an old corner shop in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo's coffee district; the owner hand-pours each cup and chats with regulars.

dish: Japanese whisky flights incl. rare Venture Whisky and Mercian bottlings
n: Zoetrope (ゾートロープ)
w: Tiny Nishi-Shinjuku whisky bar with about 300 bottles, over a hundred of them Japanese incl. sold-out limited editions; the cinephile owner screens silent films while you drink.

dish: House Endless Brown Ale from 40+ taps
n: Goodbeer Faucets Shibuya (グッドビアフォウセッツ 渋谷)
w: Shibuya craft-beer bar open since 2012 with one of the city's largest tap lists (40+ Japanese, US and European beers) and a well-known happy hour.

dish: Baird Teikoku IPA and Angry Boy Brown Ale
n: Baird Beer Nakameguro Taproom (ベアードタップルーム中目黒)
address: 2F Nakameguro Gate Town, 2-1-3 Kamimeguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
w: First Tokyo pub of Numazu's Baird Brewing, a brick-and-wood taproom pouring Baird's own beers alongside New Haven-style pizza.

dish: Azuki and meringue kakigōri (shaved ice with mochi sauce and cooked azuki)
n: Azuki to Kouri (あずきとこおり)
w: Seven-seat, reservation-only kakigōri counter in Yoyogi-Uehara opened in January 2022 by pastry chef Miho Horio (ex-Florilège); signature azuki-and-meringue shaved ice.

dish: Seasonal-fruit kakigōri accented with sake lees
n: Mamatoko (ママトコ)
w: Residential-Nakano shaved-ice shop of Asako Harada, the 'Kakigōri Queen' said to have eaten some 1,800 bowls in a year; known for mountainous, painterly bowls such as seasonal fruit with sake lees.

dish: Precisely warmed hot sake (kanzake) with a five-course omakase
n: Utsura Utsura (うつらうつら)
w: Eight-seat counter izakaya a short walk from central Shibuya; the sake sommelier is a hot-sake specialist warming each pour to a precise temperature, paired with a good-value omakase.

dish: Coffee during the twice-daily classical record 'concerts'
n: Meikyoku Kissa Lion (名曲喫茶ライオン)
w: Tokyo's oldest and best-known classical-music café, first opened in 1926 and rebuilt in 1950; pew-like seats face a 3m Pioneer speaker wall and conversation is discouraged.

dish: Drip coffee in a family-run 1954 kissaten
n: Coffee Lawn (珈琲ローン)
w: Yotsuya kissaten started in 1954 by the father of current owner Hiroaki Ogura, profiled by Monocle among Tokyo's enduring independent kissaten; a regular haunt of visiting jazz band The Lagerphones.

dish: Drinks played against an 11,000-record jazz, blues and soul vinyl wall
n: JBS (Jazz Blues Soul)
w: Small Dogenzaka record bar whose name stands for Jazz, Blues and Soul; over 11,000 LPs line the walls and the owner spins from them.

dish: Mame-daifuku (mochi with red bean paste and salty whole beans)
n: Gunrindo (群林堂)
w: Wagashi shop by Gokokuji Station renowned for its large mame-daifuku, mochi wrapped around anko with slightly salty whole beans kneaded in, still sold cheaply.

dish: Filter-coffee tasting courses from ~20 auction-lot single origins
n: Lonich (ロニッチ)
w: Kuramae specialty coffee flagship offering tasting courses and around 20 filtered coffees, many rare single origins bought at auction, with an omakase-style coffee experience.

dish: Brownie flight of three single-origin cacao cakes; hot chocolate
n: Dandelion Chocolate Factory & Café Kuramae (ダンデライオン・チョコレート 蔵前)
w: Tokyo home of the San Francisco bean-to-bar chocolatier: half café, half factory, where you watch chocolate made through the glass and order the brownie flight.

dish: Siphon coffee; 'fruit' and 'chocolate' house blends
n: Obscura Coffee Roasters — Café Obscura, Sangenjaya (オブスキュラ コーヒーロースターズ)
w: Sangenjaya roaster founded in 2009 and credited with seeding the district's specialty coffee scene; its gallery-like main café specialises in siphon coffee with two house blends and rotating single origins.
